source.title: THE EMPIRICAL COMPARISON OF DEEP NEURAL NETWORK OPTIMIZERS FOR BINARY CLASSIFICATION OF OCT IMAGES

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper. Some prose and table descriptions are internally inconsistent, but the optimizer tables are legible.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers using test accuracy and loss on an image-classification task; this tests optimizer-related generalization with a different dataset and setup from V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training accuracy, test accuracy, and train/test loss for three models, five optimizers, and three learning rates. Rows below capture every Table 5 test-accuracy result. The paper does not test random-label memorization, and its cited prior-work results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with SGD and momentum SGD on held-out OCT images, extending V4 to a medical-image setting. It reports results after 10 epochs at three learning rates, without establishing convergence or equivalent tuning across optimizers.
record.authors_conclusion: The record understates the authors' conclusion: they claim Adam is the most effective optimizer across all three models and learning rates, report 100% training accuracy at 0.001, and recommend CNN with Adam. Those broad claims are not consistently supported by their tables.
record.recipe_differences: Tests five optimizers on OCTID binary classification with CNN, DNN, and VGG16 for 10 epochs across three learning rates; reports accuracy and loss rather than a direct generalization-gap analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer rankings vary by architecture and learning rate; the text describes Adam and Adagrad as generally strong, with exceptions at particular learning rates and models.
record.problems: Only 27 test images are reported. No uncertainty estimates or controls are stated. Training accuracy is often high, but the paper does not analyze train-test gaps directly. Prose descriptions sometimes conflict with table entries, including statements about which optimizer performs best at particular learning rates.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 train-loss, Table 3 test-loss, and Table 4 training-accuracy results are not included; the 45 Table 5 test-accuracy rows were prioritized as the clearest held-out performance measure relevant to V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label generalization comparison.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.

An established comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch, and the roles of local connectivity, learned sparsity, or convolutional initialization. Architectures are described, but initialization and comparable architecture tuning are not established.

Language benchmarks, learning-rate decay schedule tuning, broader hyperparameter searches, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers. Converged or training-performance-matched comparisons are not established.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 5 values are transcribed correctly, including the questionable 81.89%. The principal extraction error is reversing V4's direction: higher adaptive accuracy contradicts the named disadvantage. Verdicts concern specific tested conditions and do not refute the qualified claim that adaptive methods often perform worse elsewhere. Only 27 test images are reported, including 21 normal images; 77.78% equals the majority-class baseline, although predictions are unavailable. No uncertainty estimates are supplied. R43 is excluded from verdict evidence because of its internally questionable value. Tables 2–4 are explicitly declared omitted, so they do not require missing entries. For example, Table 3 shows DNN Adam test loss of 0.1984 versus SGD's 0.0435 at 0.001 despite equal training and test accuracy; accuracy ties therefore do not establish equivalent performance on every measure.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and matched training performance/generalization gaps.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptation of large-batch training recipes.
Sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.

relationships.condition: DNN: RMSprop at learning rate 0.001; all three adaptive methods at 0.00001, after 10 epochs
relationships.reason: R19 and R28–R30 report 77.78% test accuracy versus 81.48–96.29% for the corresponding SGD comparators; these runs also fit the training data worse.
relationships.display_finding: Reported test accuracy favored the corresponding SGD comparators, while the adaptive runs also fit training data worse; these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CNN: Adagrad at 0.001, RMSprop at 0.001 and 0.0001, and Adam at all three learning rates
relationships.reason: R03–R05, R09–R10 and R15 show adaptive-method accuracy of 88.89–96.29% versus 77.78% for SGD and momentum SGD.
relationships.display_finding: Reported adaptive accuracies ranged from 88.89% to 96.29% versus 77.78% for SGD comparators, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: VGG16: Adam at 0.001; RMSprop and Adam at 0.00001
relationships.reason: R35 reports 100% versus 96.29% for SGD comparators; R44–R45 report 88.89% versus 77.78% and 81.48%.
relationships.display_finding: Adam and RMSprop reportedly exceeded SGD comparators at the specified learning rates, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CNN: Adagrad at 0.0001 and 0.00001, RMSprop at 0.00001; DNN: Adagrad and Adam at 0.001, all adaptive methods at 0.0001; VGG16: Adagrad and RMSprop at 0.001, all adaptive methods at 0.0001
relationships.reason: R08, R13–R14, R18, R20, R23–R25, R33–R34 and R38–R40 tie their SGD comparators, showing no adaptive-optimizer test-accuracy penalty in these conditions.
relationships.display_finding: The specified adaptive methods reportedly tied their SGD comparators, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: OCTID binary OCT classification, 10 epochs, CNN/DNN/VGG16, tested learning rates
reader_labels.reason: Adaptive methods often equal or exceed SGD and momentum SGD test accuracy in these conditions (R01–R45), including several ties and some reversals; this challenges a general tendency for adaptive methods to perform worse.
